step1_analysis.description: An LC-degenerated emitter-coupled pair that acts as an active balun and low-noise amplifier. It converts a single-ended RF input to a differential output while providing low-noise amplification at high frequencies.

paper_reference.title: A 20-GHz Low-Noise Amplifier With Active Balun in a 0.25-m SiGe BICMOS Technology

center_frequency.description: Frequency at which the amplifier achieves maximum gain.

sky130_expected.calculation: Determined by the LC tank resonance: f = 1 / (2 * pi * sqrt(L * C)). Tuned to 20 GHz.
sky130_expected.reasoning: The LC tank can be sized to resonate at 20 GHz in SKY130, though parasitic capacitances will require smaller explicit capacitors.

voltage_gain.description: Maximum differential voltage gain at the center frequency.

sky130_expected.calculation: Gain ~ gm * Z_tank. For Id=5mA, gm~50mS. Z_tank at 20GHz is limited by low Q of inductors in CMOS.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SKY130 NMOS has lower fT and transconductance compared to SiGe BJTs, resulting in lower achievable gain at 20 GHz.

power_consumption.description: Total DC power consumed from the supply.

sky130_expected.calculation: P = VDD * I_total. Assuming 10 mA total current from 1.8V supply.
sky130_expected.reasoning: Scaled down for 1.8V VDD in SKY130, maintaining sufficient current for high-frequency gm.

noise_figure.description: Signal-to-noise ratio degradation through the amplifier.

sky130_expected.calculation: CMOS NFmin at 20GHz is typically 3-4 dB. Active balun adds noise from the common-source/common-gate paths.
sky130_expected.reasoning: SiGe BJTs have superior noise performance at mm-wave frequencies compared to 130nm CMOS.

amplitude_imbalance.description: Ratio of the magnitudes of the two single-ended outputs.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Active baluns typically achieve <1 dB imbalance near resonance.

phase_difference.description: Phase difference between the two single-ended outputs.

sky130_expected.reasoning: Degeneration and parasitic mismatches cause slight deviations from the ideal 180 degrees.

step3_testbench.description: Testbench to measure DC power, AC voltage gain, center frequency, amplitude imbalance, and phase difference of the active balun LNA.
step3_testbench.spice:
* 20-GHz LNA with Active Balun Testbench
.lib "${SKY130_PDK}" tt

* Generic NPN model for simulation since SKY130 parasitic NPNs are too slow for 20GHz
.model npn NPN(IS=1e-16 BF=100 VAF=50 CJC=10f CJE=20f TF=5p)

* DUT (with added component values for simulation)
Q2 Vout_plus Vin N_EMIT npn
Q3 Vout_minus VIN2 N_EMIT npn
Ce2 N_EMIT GND 100f
Lc2 VDD Vout_plus 1n
Lc3 VDD Vout_minus 1n
V1 Vout_plus VOUT_P 0
Le2 N_EMIT GND 0.5n
V2 VOUT_N Vout_minus 0

* Load Capacitors
Cload1 VOUT_P GND 50f
Cload2 VOUT_N GND 50f

* Biasing and Sources
VVDD VDD 0 1.8
* Vin is the RF input, VIN2 is AC grounded for active balun operation
VVIN VIN 0 DC 0.9 AC 1
VVIN2 VIN2 0 DC 0.9 AC 0

.control
op
let power = -i(VVDD) * 1.8
print power

ac dec 100 1G 100G
let vout_diff = v(VOUT_P) - v(VOUT_N)
let gain_db = 20*log10(mag(vout_diff))
let amp_imb_db = 20*log10(mag(v(VOUT_P)) / mag(v(VOUT_N)))
let phase_diff = 180/PI * (cph(v(VOUT_P)) - cph(v(VOUT_N)))

meas ac max_gain max gain_db
meas ac gain_at_20G find gain_db at=20G
meas ac amp_imb_at_20G find amp_imb_db at=20G
meas ac phase_diff_at_20G find phase_diff at=20G

quit
.endc
.end
